description: Race events are held at a circuit and cannot exist without one; the circuit is the whole of which the events held there are parts.
A season is made up of the race events of that year; a race event belongs to exactly one season.
The classification of a race is composed of the result entries of the drivers who took part in it.
A result entry is part of a driver's record and is meaningless without the driver it belongs to.
A result entry is also part of a constructor's record, because each entry is made with one constructor's car.
The qualifying session is a component of a race event weekend and its entries cannot exist without the race event.
Pit stops occur inside a race event and are meaningless outside it.
A pit stop belongs to the driver who made it.
An accident is one specific value of the race status vocabulary, a subtype of the outcomes a race entry can have.
Having finished the race is one specific value of the race status vocabulary.
The winner of a race is a specific case of a driver who finished the race; the value set of winners is a subset of the value set of finishers.

connection_condition: drivers.driverId and drivers.driverRef are two key forms of the same driver row
description: The numeric key and the reference string denote the same driver; the reference string is the human-readable form of the same identity.
A driver's full name is derived from the driver's stored name parts: the given name and the family name joined in that order.
A driver's average pit stop duration is derived by averaging that driver's individual stop durations.
The fastest lap of a race is derived as the minimum lap time recorded by each driver in that race, and the rank of a driver's fastest lap is derived by ordering those minima.
A driver's cumulative standing is derived by accumulating the per-race points that driver was awarded across the season.
A constructor's cumulative standing is derived by accumulating the per-race points credited to that constructor across the season.

connection_condition: drivers.nationality holds the affiliation as a text value with no reference to a country table
description: A driver has a nationality affiliation recorded as free text, related to the country concepts used elsewhere in the data only through the meaning of the value.

connection_condition: constructors.nationality holds the affiliation as a text value with no reference to a country table
description: A constructor has a nationality affiliation recorded as free text, in the same demonym vocabulary as driver nationality.

connection_condition: circuits.country and the nationality columns both name places but use different vocabularies: country names against demonyms
description: The country of a circuit describes the same kind of affiliation as a nationality, but the two vocabularies are not aligned, so they are related semantically rather than through shared values.

connection_condition: a race event reaches its coordinates indirectly, through races.circuitId and circuits.lat/lng
description: The location coordinates of a race event are those of the circuit that hosted it; the connection is indirect.
The outcome code classifies how a result entry ended and is shared by many entries, so it is a category associated with the entry rather than a component of it.

connection_condition: the encoding of the time value is determined by whether the entry is the first-placed one
description: The meaning of a recorded race time depends on the finishing position of the entry: the first-placed entry carries an absolute duration while the others carry gaps to it.
